entities.summary: Marceli Godlewski was a Polish priest who saved Jews during the Holocaust by hiding them, assisting in escapes, and issuing fake baptismal certificates. From 1915 until 1945, Fr. Monsignor Godlewski was a priest in Warsaw's All Saints parish, which became part of the Warsaw Ghetto in 1940. In this position, he was actively involved in helping Jews during the German occupation of Poland, for which he was posthumously awarded the medal of the Righteous Among the Nations in 2009. He was also a prelate, social activist, National Democrat politician and member of the Polish National Committee (1914–1917).

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Fr. Marceli Godlewski's heroic actions saved hundreds of Jews during the Holocaust, and his work as a priest in Warsaw's All Saints parish had significant regional impact on the Jewish community in Poland.
